name: sol_token_fe_10
description: Calling token transfer/transferFrom with a zero amount without guarding, risking revert on tokens that reject zero-value transfers
question: The source file in `source` calls an ERC20 `transfer` or `transferFrom` function with an amount value that may be zero, without first checking that the amount is greater than zero, so integration with tokens that revert on zero-amount transfers would cause the whole operation to unexpectedly fail.
criteria: A function calls `token.transfer(recipient, amount)` where `amount` can be zero (e.g. computed from a fee, reward, or difference calculation) with no prior `if (amount == 0) return;` or `require(amount > 0)` check
A loop iterates over multiple recipients calling `token.transferFrom(msg.sender, recipients[i], amounts[i])` without skipping or checking entries where `amounts[i] == 0`
A reward or interest distribution function calls `transfer` with an amount derived from a calculation that can legitimately evaluate to zero, without a zero-amount guard before the transfer call
A withdrawal or sweep function forwards the entire `balanceOf(address(this))` via `transfer` without checking that the balance is nonzero before calling transfer
